resources.string: Milk flow in a mammary gland
Qualitative cross-section of one lactating alveolus and its adjoining duct. Shape, motion and timing are illustrative, not to scale or predictions of milk volume or flow.
Luminal epithelial cells line the milk space. Myoepithelial cells lie outside that lining, and the lumen opens into a duct.
Luminal epithelial cells release milk components from the side that faces the alveolar lumen.
Secreted milk collects in the alveolar lumen before ejection. The shading shows accumulation qualitatively.
In response to oxytocin, the outer myoepithelial cells contract and squeeze the alveolus.
The squeeze moves milk from the alveolar lumen into the adjoining duct.
